jsesh.mdcDisplayer.mdcView
Class MDCView

java.lang.Object
  jsesh.mdcDisplayer.mdcView.MDCView
public class MDCView
extends java.lang.Object

Base class for all view elements. A view element is a view of an MDC model element. THIS IS AN ATTEMPT AT A SIMPLER VIEW CLASS.

About coordinates : we take hereby the convention that the y axis is oriented bottomward (as in so-called "text mode").

Note that the view class is not intended to be "intelligent". The methods available are quite numerous, but very, very basic. The layout is done by the layout classes. In particular, no reference is made nor should be made in this class to DrawingSpecification.

A view's coordinates are expressed in the reference system of its container view. A view, as a container, can be oriented left-to-right or right-to-left (I don't see currently any interest for top-to-bottom vs. bottom-to-top). In left-to-right-system, 0,0 is the top-left part of the container view, and the coordinates designate the top-left corner of the subview. In right-to-left system, 0,0 is the top-right corner, the coordinates designate the top-right corner of the subview, and the x axis is oriented to the right, as far as views go. Drawing will take place in the normal way (? is this a good idea ?).

any view contains the following information :

Scaling and dimensions : scaling and dimensions are really two different things in this class. An important thing to note is that a view's dimensions are quite independant of those of its subviews. So, scaling a view won't modify its width or height. If one wants a view to be just large enough for its subviews, one should call fitToSubViews(), after all subviews have been placed and computed. If some subview is modified thereafter, fitToSubViews() should be called once more.

deltaBaseLine and deltaBaseColumn are modifiers which describe the difference between the "standard" base lines and column and those for this view. Normally, the tops of the views are aligned in horizontal text. Note that those values are used for computing the position of the view. Once this is done, the position is completely defined.

fitToSubViews

public void fitToSubViews(boolean doTranslate)
Compute the dimensions of this view so that it contains exactly its subviews.

If doTranslate is true, the subviews will be moved; else they won't, and the view might actually be larger than needed.

Parameters:
doTranslate - if true, subviews will be translated.
